title: Optimized protocol for quantification of mitochondrial non-heme and heme iron content in mouse tissues and cultured cells
protocol: Weigh frozen whole cerebral cortex tissues and cut into ∼50 mg sections using a blade on a pre-chilled platform with dry ice.
Place the cortex sections into pre-chilled 2.0 mL tubes (tubes A).
Keep tubes A in liquid nitrogen or on dry ice until all samples to be analyzed have been processed.
Prepare Reagent A and Reagent C solutions in the mitochondria isolation kit and add 1/100 volume of protease inhibitors to each solution.
Add ice cold 500 μL Reagent A solution into tubes A.
Perform homogenization using a Polytron Tissue Grinder (shaft size: 5.5 mm, speed: high) for 30 s while on ice.
Clean the tip of the homogenizer with 70% EtOH once and ddH2O twice between samples to minimize sample-to-sample contamination in the homogenization.
Visually check if there are any tissue fragments left after homogenization; extend the homogenization time by 30 s and reassess if tissues are not sufficiently homogenized.
Collect cells in 15 mL conical tubes.
Wash the cell suspension twice in ice cold PBS.
Transfer the washed cell suspension to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 1,000 g to pellet the cells (Tube A).
Discard the supernatant from Tube A.
Prepare Reagent A and Reagent C solutions with protease inhibitors added.
Add 500 μL of ice cold Reagent A solution into Tube A.
Add 6.25 μL of Reagent B solution into Tube A.
Vortex vigorously for 5 seconds every minute for 5 minutes.
Add 500 μL of Reagent C to Tube A and mix thoroughly.
Centrifuge tubes at 700 g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the pellet from tubes.
Transfer the supernatant into new 2.0 mL tubes (tubes B).
Centrifuge tubes B at 3,000 g for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant from tube B to a new 1.5 mL tube (tube C) as cytosolic fraction.
Wash the pellet with 250 μL of Reagent C and centrifuge tubes at 3,000 g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Add 200 μL of PBS containing 1% Triton X-100 and 1× Protease Arrest to the pellet from tube B.
Take 10 μL of each fraction for BCA protein assay.
Freeze lysates at −20°C for a month or use directly for subsequent measurements.
Mix 5 mL of 1 N HCl with 5 mL of 10% Trichloroacetic acid to prepare the protein precipitation solution (PPS).
Store PPS at 4°C for up to one week.
Dissolve 2.5 mg of Ferrozine and 1.2 g of sodium acetate in 10 mL ddH2O.
Add 10 μL of thioglycolic acid to the solution prepared in the previous step to create the chromogen solution (CS).
Prepare CS fresh for each assay.
Mix 80 μL of either cytosolic or mitochondrial lysate fraction with 80 μL of PPS in a 1.5 mL tube.
Vortex the mixture well at room temperature.
Heat tubes in a heating block at 95°C for one hour.
Use cap locks to prevent tubes from opening and solution from evaporating during heating.
During the heating step, dilute 1 mM FeSO4 solution in PPS in 1.5 mL tubes for standards (0 μM, 0.25 μM, 0.5 μM, 1.0 μM, 2.5 μM, 5 μM, 10 μM, 25 μM).
Place the diluted standards on ice for 2 min.
Centrifuge the standards and tubes D at 16,000 g at 4°C for 10 min.
Take 100 μL of standards or supernatant from tubes D and place into a single well of clear 96-well assay plates.
Add 100 μL of CS into the lysate per well of a 96-well assay plate.
Incubate at room temperature for 10 min.
Measure absorbance at 562 nm using a plate reader.
Normalize values by dividing the amount of iron in 1 μL of sample by the amount of protein in 1 μL assessed by BCA method.
If crystals precipitate in oxalic acid, heat in the microwave for 5 seconds to dissolve the crystal before use.
Mix 100 μL of lysates from the cytosolic or mitochondrial fraction with 100 μL of warm OS in 1.5 mL tubes.
Vigorously vortex at room temperature.
Dissolve 6.5 mg of hemin in 1 mL of DMSO to create a 10 mM hemin solution.
Dilute 10 μL of the 10 mM hemin solution in 990 μL warm OS to prepare a 100 μM hemin standard.
Heat heme-iron samples and heme standards in a heating block at 90°C for 30 minutes.
Centrifuge samples and standards at 700 g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Dilute 100 μM heme standards in a 1:1 mixture of OS and PBS with 1% Triton to desired concentrations.
Transfer 150 μL of supernatant or diluted heme standards into black-walled clear bottom 96-well plates.
Quantify fluorescence at an excitation wavelength of 405 nm and an emission wavelength of 600 nm.
Normalize values by dividing the amount of iron in 1 μL of sample by the amount of protein in 1 μL assessed by BCA method.
